tax.text: He supports replacing the federal income tax with a national consumption tax while reducing the federal government's size and role.
tax.quote: He also advocates replacing the federal income tax with a national consumption tax, arguing it would create a simpler, fairer system that rewards work instead of penalizing it.

debt.text: He supports balancing the federal budget by cutting military spending and shifting some federal responsibilities to states, communities, and private organizations.
debt.quote: He supports balancing the federal budget by reducing military spending, ending U.S. involvement in wars that are not purely defensive, and shifting more responsibility to states, local communities, and private organizations where they can provide services more effectively.

immigration.text: He supports expanding legal immigration pathways while maintaining secure borders and protecting civil liberties during enforcement.
immigration.quote: Maad also supports reforming immigration by expanding legal pathways while maintaining secure borders and enforcing immigration laws in a way that protects civil liberties.

health.text: He supports a public safety net for catastrophic medical events alongside private-sector solutions for routine care.
health.quote: He believes no American should face financial ruin because of a catastrophic medical event and supports maintaining a public safety net for extraordinary circumstances while encouraging private-sector solutions for routine care.

tax.text: Rouzer says lower taxes promote job growth and supported the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act.
tax.quote: Lower taxes lead to job growth and a healthy economy as employees and employers keep more of their earnings to save, spend, and invest.

wages.text: Rouzer opposed raising the federal minimum wage.
wages.quote: Rouzer said he opposed raising the minimum wage.

trade.text: Rouzer joined a bipartisan letter seeking stronger enforcement against tariff evasion to protect the U.S. textile industry.
trade.quote: Congressional Textile Caucus Co-Chairs Reps. David Rouzer (R-NC-07) and Adriano Espaillat (D-NY-13), joined by fourteen Members of Congress, sent a bipartisan letter to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security urging stronger customs enforcement measures to protect the American textile industry from fraudulent trade practices and illegal imports.

housing.text: Rouzer supported legislation removing federal regulations that he said increased homebuilding costs.
housing.quote: With my support, the House also passed the Affordable HOMES Act (H.R. 5184) to slash unnecessary federal regulations that make homebuilding more expensive than it otherwise would be.

schools.text: Rouzer says parents should have the right to choose where their children attend school.
schools.quote: I believe every parent should have the right to choose where they send their children to school.

safety.text: Rouzer supported legislation providing grants to hire 100,000 additional police officers.
safety.quote: This legislation would provide grant funding to hire an additional 100,000 police officers within the next five years.

guns.text: Rouzer supported overturning the federal pistol-brace rule and pledged to defend gun-ownership rights.
guns.quote: I'm proud to support the effort to overturn this rule and will continue fighting to protect Americans' fundamental right to bear arms.

abortion.text: Rouzer praised the Dobbs ruling and pledged continued support for anti-abortion measures in Congress.
abortion.quote: Today’s ruling is a significant win for life, and I will continue to support pro-life measures in Congress.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: Rouzer voted for legislation barring transgender women and girls from competing in female sports.
gender.quote: The House, with my support, voted to pass a bill protecting the integrity of women’s sports by banning transgender males from competing with female athletes.

cannabis.text: Rouzer voted against the MORE Act and said federal legalization would endanger communities.
cannabis.quote: I voted against this bill because it would result in greater widespread marijuana use and sale in America allowing bad actors and criminal organizations to further exploit the nation’s drug addiction crisis.

health.text: Rouzer favors competition, transparency, and keeping government officials out of individual health-care decisions.
health.quote: The American people deserve a solution, and we must create a framework for competition and transparency that will foster a healthcare system that provides the very best care at the lowest possible price.

energy.text: Rouzer supports expanding domestic energy production to provide affordable energy and reduce foreign dependence.
energy.quote: I will continuously advocate and vote to increase domestic production so we have affordable energy that is produced in America, so we are not reliant upon others.

voting.text: Rouzer supported the SAVE America Act, including federal photo-identification, citizenship-documentation, and voter-roll requirements.
voting.quote: This past week, with my support, the House passed the SAVE America Act, which builds on the integrity measures of the SAVE Act by also including a photo ID requirement for federal elections to further protect our republic from election fraud.

tax.text: Hardy proposed taxing the wealthiest 1% to fund public programs while also offering tax relief below certain incomes.
tax.quote: I have a solution to paying for a lot of these things, which is to tax the wealthiest 1%.

wages.text: Hardy supports raising the federal minimum wage and strengthening overtime protections.
wages.quote: Raising the federal minimum wage for the first time in nearly 30 years.

trade.text: Hardy said tariffs are harming agricultural exports and should be rolled back.
trade.quote: These tariffs, for example, are really, really bad for exports.

debt.text: Hardy pledges to protect Medicare and Medicaid rather than cut those programs.
debt.quote: Protect Medicare and Medicaid and fight to keep health insurance premiums affordable and coverage meaningful.

schools.text: Hardy supports federal investment in local public schools and programs administered through the Department of Education.
schools.quote: I will be a strong voice in making sure that wherever you live in southeast NC, you have local public schools

health.text: Hardy says reversing federal Medicaid cuts would be one of her first priorities in Congress.
health.quote: the first thing I want to do is roll back these Medicaid cuts.
